idiom_name: struct members + sqlite3_bind_*/sqlite3_column_* per column, or libpq PQexecParams
implementation_notes: ISO C has neither value semantics nor a mapper, so the classic structure survives in full: the value type is a plain struct with no id member, and the decompose/recompose pair is a handful of sqlite3_bind_* calls on write and sqlite3_column_* calls on read, one per field of the value (or one entry each in the paramValues array of PQexecParams). The column-name prefix convention replaces the mapper's naming strategy: the owner's member name becomes the prefix, so total_amount_minor and total_currency belong to order.total. The classic form is not merely justified but the only option; a code generator or an ORM with composite-value support (ODB, sqlite-orm) is worth adopting when several value types are shared across many tables.
pitfalls: Binding a pointer to the value's own memory with SQLITE_STATIC means the buffer must outlive the statement; use SQLITE_TRANSIENT when the value is a temporary and let SQLite copy it.
sqlite3_column_text returns a pointer that is invalidated by the next type conversion, step or reset on that statement - copy the field out before touching another column.
A struct memcpy into the row, or a char[] field without an explicit length rule, silently stores padding and host byte order; each field needs its own column and its own conversion.
